key_findings.finding: A single direct comparative neonatal clinical study (PMID 27519933; Acta Ophthalmologica, 2017) was identified: prospective randomized double-blind within-infant study of 30 premature infants, with one eye receiving three drops of tropicamide 0.5% (TTT) and the fellow eye receiving one drop phenylephrine 5% plus two drops tropicamide 0.5% (PTT). The accessible abstract identifies the participants as premature infants but does not report gestational age, postnatal age, or birth-weight distributions.

source_tools.relevance: Direct study design, sample size, and dosing

key_findings.finding: The combination produced substantially greater normalized pupil diameter: pupil diameter/cornea diameter 65.9% ± 8.8% with PTT versus 47.3% ± 8.7% with TTT, an absolute difference of 18.6 percentage points (approximately 1.39-fold), p<0.0001.

source_tools.relevance: Direct efficacy endpoint and statistical significance

key_findings.finding: The combination produced nearly twice the normalized pupil surface area: pupil surface/cornea surface 43.8% ± 7.3% with PTT versus 23.1% ± 8.3% with TTT, an absolute difference of 20.7 percentage points and ratio 1.90, p<0.0001. Thus, the claim of approximately twice the efficacy is accurate for pupil surface area, not for linear pupil diameter.

source_tools.relevance: Direct surface-area endpoint, ratio, and significance

key_findings.finding: Retinal examination adequacy was also better with the combination: retinal periphery visualization was possible in 30/30 PTT eyes versus 16/30 TTT eyes (100% vs 53.3%; absolute difference 46.7 percentage points), p<0.0001.

source_tools.relevance: Direct clinical examination endpoint and significance
